title: AMALI: An Analytical Model for Accurately Modeling LLM Inference on Modern GPUs
problem: Existing GPU analytical models cannot accurately predict LLM inference performance because they mismodel tensor core throughput, ignore constant and instruction cache effects, and abstract away warp-level execution details critical to LLM kernels.
motivation: Architects rely on analytical models to quickly identify bottlenecks and explore design spaces; errors exceeding 100% MAPE in current models make them unreliable for LLM inference workloads on modern GPUs such as A100.
method: AMALI introduces three modeling innovations: (1) an instruction-modifier and throughput-based tensor core model that captures math-pipe throttle stalls by accurately modeling the pipeline fill/drain behavior of tensor cores; (2) micro-benchmark-derived analytical models for constant cache and instruction cache that measure CUDA kernel launching latencies; (3) a multi-warp model using warp instruction number distributions to reflect the heterogeneous occupancy and scheduling behavior of LLM inference kernels. All three components are validated against real A100 hardware measurements.
key_novelty: The explicit modeling of instruction-cache and constant-cache latencies via micro-benchmarks, combined with a throttle-stall-aware tensor core model, reduces LLM inference MAPE from 127.56% to 23% on A100.
contributions: Instruction-modifier and throughput-based tensor core model capturing math-pipe throttle stalls
Analytical constant-cache and instruction-cache models derived from CUDA micro-benchmarks
Multi-warp execution model using warp instruction number distribution for LLM inference characteristics
Validation on A100 GPU reducing MAPE from 127.56% to 23% across typical LLM inference applications

metrics.accuracy: MAPE reduced from 127.56% to 23% on A100

baselines: existing GPU analytical models (prior work, MAPE ~127.56%)
limitations: Validation is limited to A100 GPU; applicability to other GPU microarchitectures (e.g., H100 with Hopper SM) requires additional micro-benchmark re-characterization.
primary_theme: analytical GPU performance modeling for LLM inference
